title: Europe’s Winter of Discontent
content: Although it is true that European integration has always been forged through crisis, the continent’s postwar story was largely one of incremental responses to relatively manageable challenges. Today, the European Union is facing multiple, interrelated problems that challenge its very raison d’être.

In toppling their own country's strongman, Serbia's new student-led opposition offers important lessons for those defending democracy elsewhere.

content: Addressing AI safety risks depends on close collaboration between the two leading AI powers, and the establishment of an incident-reporting channel is just a small step in this direction. But success will require that the US and Chinese governments actually understand what is happening under their own noses.

title: The Authoritarian Logic of Selective Privacy
content: Around the world, governments are increasingly deciding who gets privacy and who is denied it, a double standard that turns a fundamental democratic right into a privilege. US President Donald Trump’s administration is a prime example, shielding ICE agents from scrutiny while expanding surveillance of immigrants and protesters.

title: PS Events: Reinventing Europe – Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
content: When we talk about "reinvention" we often overlook what works, noted WTO Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala in her closing keynote. This is true of the global trading system, which has proven surprisingly resilient in recent years, and of the European economy, which might not have a tech giant to rival those in the US or China, but remains a global trade powerhouse and a leader in science and research. While Europe has much to do to improve its external competitiveness, it must not act from a sense of panic. Instead, it must pursue measured reforms and seize new opportunities, not least closer trade and investment ties with Africa.

content: Extreme weather and climate-related events caused €822 billion in economic losses across the European Union between 1980 and 2024, with a quarter of the losses occurring just in the last five years.
